content.thinking:
I'm trying to pin down the exact dhatu "रुगिँ" in the dhatupatha, checking it against similar nearby roots like लगिँ, अगिँ, वगिँ to confirm which one takes नुम् as an इदित् root.

Given it's इदित्, I derive रुङ्ग् as the parasmaipada base. Then I work through यङ् formation with reduplication to get रोरुङ्ग्य, apply णिच् with the य-lopa rule after a consonant stem to reach रोरुङ्गि, and finally add सन् with इट् to arrive at रोरुङ्गयिष as the desiderative-causative-intensive form.

I'm working through the reduplication for सन् applied after this यङन्त-णिच् base, doubling the first vowel portion and shortening it per the rules, landing on something like रुरोरुङ्गयिष, while recalling analogous forms like बोभूयिषते/बुबोभावयिषति as a check on the pattern.

I'm uncertain whether the paribhāṣā "सन्यङोः" blocks re-doubling once a dhātu has already been reduplicated for yaṅanta, and I'm trying to recall how a tool like vidyut-prakriya would actually generate the sannanta form of this yaṅanta stem—whether it comes out as "bobhūyiṣate" or something else entirely.

I'm trying to recall whether yaṅanta dhātus taking san undergo double reduplication, and wondering whether vidyut's code has logic to skip re-doubling a term that's already been doubled once. I'm also searching my memory for traditional examples that would confirm how this case is actually treated.

Actually the sutra 6.1.9 सन्यङोः carries forward "अनभ्यासस्य" from 6.1.8, meaning a dhatu that already has an abhyasa isn't doubled again. Since बोभूय already contains an abhyasa, this constraint would apply to it when sani is added.

Tracking that "धातोरनभ्यासस्य" carries forward through 6.1.9-6.1.11, so for यङन्त + सन् forms like बोभूयिषते there's no further doubling, and working through how णिच् would combine with बोभूय to get something like बोभावयिषति or बोभूययिषति depending on the vowel/hal rules applying.

Now turning to question 1's आशीर्लिङ् in parasmaipada, प्रथम द्विवचन: since यङन्त is आत्मनेपदी but णिच् makes it ubhayapada, and सन् after a णिजन्त base follows that same ubhayapada status (पूर्ववत्सनः), parasmaipada is valid here. For आशीर्लिङ् parasmaipada I need यासुट् with कित् designation in आशिष्, giving the ardhadhatuka stem रोरुङ्गयिष (ending in अ, so अतो लोपः applies) combined with यास्.

Attaching ताम् gives रोरुङ्गयिष्यास्ताम्; since यासुट् doesn't begin with a valādi letter, इट् doesn't apply here. With the सम् upasarga, मोऽनुस्वारः converts the म् to anusvara before र, and since र has no savarna nasal, it stays as anusvara rather than converting further — giving संरोरुङ्गयिष्यास्ताम्. I want to double check the यङ् formation itself though, specifically how the अभ्यास is formed from रुङ्ग् with हलादिः शेष applying to the reduplicated syllable.

Now I'm verifying that यङ् is valid here since रुङ्ग् is a single-vowel root beginning with a consonant, satisfying एकाचो हलादेः for क्रियासमभिहार. Then applying णिच् to रोरुङ्ग्य, I'm working through यस्य हलः (6.4.49) which elides the य् after a consonant before an ardhadhatuka affix, reducing रोरुङ्ग्य + णिच् to रोरुङ्गि.

Since the upadha ङ् isn't a laghu vowel, there's no guna here, so it stays रोरुङ्गि. Moving to सन्, I add इट् since the root is सेट्, then apply guna to णि giving रोरुङ्गे, which becomes अय् before the vowel, and स changes to ष after इ — arriving at रोरुङ्गयिष, giving a candidate form संरोरुङ्गयिष्यास्ताम्, though I want to double-check the anuvṛtti of अनभ्यासस्य against a known example to be sure.

I recall from Madhaviya Dhatuvritti that "बोभूयिषते" is the attested yaṅ+san form under भू, so I'll settle on that. Moving to the next question, क्लदँ् (भ्वादि, वैक्लव्ये) has an anudātta accent marked on अ, meaning anudāttet, which signals ātmanepada.

For this root I'm working through the yaṅ formation: the abhyāsa reduces to क, applies kuhoścuḥ to get च, and the guṇa/dīrgha rules lengthen the abhyāsa vowel to आ, giving चाक्लद्य with no nuk insertion since द is non-nasal. Then applying ṇic to this yaṅanta form, the य gets elided after द्, leading toward चाक्लद् + इ.

Now I'm checking whether the उपधा vowel अ before द् should lengthen to वृद्धि आ, giving चाक्लादि, but I need to verify whether the sthānivat treatment of the elided य blocks that vṛddhi substitution via the pūrvavidhi rule.

Since the sthānī includes the consonant य्, this lopa isn't purely an ac-ādeśa, so sthānivadbhāva via 1.1.57 may not straightforwardly apply here—unlike when only अ is elided by अतो लोपः, leaving य् behind. I'm trying to recall the actual attested form for a hal-ending root like भिद् in this yaṅ-luk plus णिच् derivation to check whether upadha guṇa/vṛddhi actually occurs.

I'm weighing the ordering of अतो लोपः versus यस्य हलः at 6.4.48-49 — since both could apply to the hal-ending yaṅanta before ardhadhatuka suffixes, I need to determine which rule is para and whether one serves as apavāda to the other, checking what Kashika says on this point.

I'm comparing this to the कथि case where अतो लोपः deletes the अ of कथ before णिच्, and sthānivat-bhāva blocks upadha vriddhi, keeping it कथयति rather than काथयति. I'm trying to recall whether a similar sthānivat principle governs the lopa of य in "यस्य हलः" constructions, checking whether this falls under 1.1.57's scope for ac-ādeśa, and searching my memory of Siddhānta Kaumudī and Kāśikā for an explicit treatment of this specific yaṅanta/ṇic case.

I'm wondering whether the lopa of the whole "य" syllable counts as an ac-ādeśa under 1.1.57, since the saṅghāta contains a vowel — checking analogous cases like पटयति (उ-lopa) and स्रजयति (विन्-lopa) where only part of the affix is elided to see if the same logic applies here.

I'm trying to recall whether the saṅghāta includes ac, searching for reliable examples like "वैयाकरणः" or yaṅanta + ṇic forms such as "बोभूययति" or "पापाचयति" from traditional sources, though nothing feels certain. I'm also trying to recall the relevant Siddhānta Kaumudī rule number and its exact wording on this point.

Now I recall it more clearly: by 1.1.54 "आदेः परस्य", only the initial य् is elided, then अतो लोपः removes the अ, and since the elided element is treated as sthānivat, the लघूपधगुण doesn't apply, yielding the form "बेभिदिता."

Right, so the laghūpadha guṇa would normally trigger here, but since it's blocked by sthānivad-bhāva of the अ-lopa, the form stays बेभिदिता rather than बेभेदिता. By the same logic, the upadha vriddhi condition under 7.2.116 for णिच् gets blocked too via 1.1.57's pūrvavidhi treatment, confirming चाक्लदि as correct.

Now moving to लुङ् with णिच् - चाक्लदि + चङ् + लुङ्, I need to work through णि-lopa by णेरनिटि and whether चङ् reduplication applies given the dhatu already carries an abhyāsa, plus the upadha-shortening rule 7.4.1 for चङ् formations.

I'm trying to recall the Kashika example meant to illustrate "अनभ्यासस्य" — maybe it relates to sannanta+णिच्+लुङ् forms like "अबुभूषत्" where no extra doubling occurs, though I'm not fully certain of the exact citation.

Working through the derivation for उत्तम द्विवचन of लुङ् for "वि+चाक्लद्": applying चङ् with the उत्तम द्विवचन ending वस्, with dīrgha applying before the यञ् ending, giving "अचाक्लदाव" as the resulting form.

I'm checking whether णौ चङ्युपधायाः ह्रस्वः applies to the upadha of चाक्लद् — since it's already short, no change is needed, and confirming kuhoścuḥ converts the abhyāsa क to च, giving चाक्लद्य, so the final form comes to व्यचाक्लदाव.

Moving to question 3 with नर्द् (भ्वादि, शब्दे, parasmaipadī) — I'm verifying it's not a णोपदेश root since it's excluded from that list, so no णत्व applies, and now I'm working out the यङ् formation for नर्द्.

For यङ्, the abhyāsa takes न (reduplication with र् dropped), giving नानर्द्य after applying गुण and दीर्घ rules, since the upadha र् doesn't trigger the ऋत्-specific rule. Then for णिच्, the य् of णिच् is elided giving नानर्दि, and I'm now setting up the सन् formation with इट् augment on नानर्दि.

For णिच्-सन्, I get नानर्दयिष without reduplication since there's no re-doubling here. Moving to लुट् first person plural, I'm working through तास् + झि, applying रस्-replacement and the इट् augment appropriate for a सन्नन्त stem (which is anekāc and सेट्), arriving at उपनानर्दयिषितारः, while checking that the इट् rule for सन्नन्त forms in ardhadhātuka contexts like बुभूषि- applies correctly here.

Now I'm tackling question 4 with the root ष्टिघँ् (स्वादि, meaning आस्कन्दने), which is anudāttet and आत्मनेपदी; the षोपदेश converts it to स्तिघ् through the ष्→स and ष्ट→स्त rules once the conditioning cause disappears. For the यङ् formation, I'm building the अभ्यास, retaining खय् in the reduplicated syllable, applying गुण to get ते, and working out how the स् (originally from ष्, treated as an आदेश) interacts with the preceding इण् vowel of the अभ्यास.

I'm checking whether 8.3.59 आदेशप्रत्ययोः triggers षत्व here, since तेष्टिघ्य would then undergo ष्टुत्व (त→ट). But I'm also weighing 8.3.61, which restricts अभ्यास-triggered षत्व specifically to सन् forms involving स्तौति or णि-endings — so I need to determine whether that restriction excludes यङ् from this षत्व altogether.

Applying ष्टुत्व gives तेष्टिघ्य, then adding णिच् with sthānivat lopa blocking guṇa yields तेष्टिघि, similar to बेभिदिता. Now I need to form लुङ् for first person singular parasmaipada, then check the चङ् (luṅ with णिच्) reduplication pattern.

Working through चङ् with no doubling since it's अनभ्यास, the upadha इ stays short, giving अभ्यतेष्टिघः as the final form after adding the अभि prefix and augment. I want to verify against the traditional yaṅanta+ṇic+luṅ example to confirm this reduplication treatment is correct.

I'm trying to recall the exact counterexample in the Kāśikā regarding "anabhyāsasya" — possibly it concerns avoiding double reduplication when a yaṅluganta form already has one, like "बोभवांचकार" with लिट्, but I'm not fully certain of the precise citation.

The underlying principle seems clear though: once a form is already reduplicated (like dhātus such as जागृ or दरिद्रा that carry lexical reduplication without technical abhyāsa-saṃjñā), it still undergoes normal doubling since it isn't abhyāsa in the technical sense — compare जजागार, ददरिद्रौ, and similar sannanta forms like अचिकीर्षत्. For the vṛddhi question, I'm settling on no, because of sthānivadbhāva.

Working through the remaining forms: Q4 gives अभ्यतेष्टिघः after applying guṇa to the abhyāsa following yaṅ (गुणो यङ्लुकोः), Q2's abhyāsa becomes चा via दीर्घोऽकितः, and Q3 yields उपनानर्दयिषितारः with the उप prefix. For Q1 I'm checking संरोरुङ्गयिष्यास्ताम् and the sandhi of सं + र into म्, along with the उपध ङ् in रोरुङ्ग् which holds regardless.
